title: REST APIs
summary: Covers the full set of HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) through Axios, comparing promise chaining with async/await. The exercise wires up a small Express + EJS app so five form buttons each call a different endpoint of the Secrets API using a bearer token.

concepts.heading: Two ways to consume a promise
points: Axios returns a promise. It can be handled with .then() / .catch() / .finally() chained on the call, or with async/await inside a try/catch.
With .then(), the callback runs once the promise resolves, and further .then() calls run in order. Long chains get hard to trace when debugging.

async/await (added to JavaScript in ES2017/ES8) marks a function async and puts await before the call, so execution pauses on that line until the promise settles and the code reads top to bottom like synchronous code.
Both styles are documented by Axios and are equivalent; the course standardises on async/await with try/catch.

concepts.heading: Axios method signatures
points: axios.get(url[, config]) and axios.delete(url[, config]): two parameters, the URL and an optional config object.

axios.post(url[, data[, config]]), axios.put(url[, data[, config]]) and axios.patch(url[, data[, config]]): three parameters. The middle one is the request body (Axios docs call it data), like the URL-encoded fields a browser form would submit.

The config object is where authentication goes, e.g. headers with an Authorization value, plus other options from the Request Config docs: url, method, baseURL, params, auth (basic auth) and so on. A request can even be described entirely in the config instead of passing the URL first.
In the docs, square brackets mark the optional parameters of each alias.

concepts.heading: What each verb means in a REST API
points: GET reads a resource.
POST creates a resource; the server usually assigns the id.
PUT replaces an existing resource, so the full set of fields must be sent; anything omitted is overwritten.
PATCH updates only the fields supplied and leaves the rest untouched.
DELETE removes the resource; no body is sent.
An API that supports all of these is called fully RESTful.

concepts.heading: The demo app and how it is wired
points: The app is an Express server that renders index.ejs. A content variable is injected into the page, so every route re-renders the template with the stringified API response (or the error).
The form has three inputs: id, secret and score. Which inputs matter depends on the route (GET/DELETE need only the id; POST needs secret and score; PUT/PATCH need the id plus the fields to change).

Five submit buttons live in one form. Each button has its own formaction attribute, which overrides the form's action for that button, so the same form posts to /get-secret, /post-secret, /put-secret, /patch-secret or /delete-secret.
All five browser requests are HTML form POSTs to the Express server. The server then makes the real GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE call to the remote API with Axios.
Input names match the field names the Secrets API expects (secret, score), so req.body can be forwarded as the request body unchanged. body-parser's urlencoded middleware populates req.body.
Default secrets run from id 1 to 50. Creating one yields id 51; the demo then reads it, PUTs a new score, PATCHes the score again, deletes it and confirms a GET now returns an error.

concepts.heading: Error handling pattern
points: On success, result.data holds the API's JSON body; JSON.stringify turns it into text for the template.
On failure Axios throws; error.response.data holds the message the API sent back (for example not found for a missing id), which is rendered the same way so the user sees what went wrong.
(Extra) If the server is unreachable there is no error.response, so reading error.response.data would itself throw; a production version would guard for that.

concepts.heading: Read the docs first
points: Before using any API, read the endpoints being used: required URL, params, body keys, auth, and the shape of the response. This prevents confusing errors later.

task.name: 5.5 REST APIs: finish the four missing routes
task.starting_point: Download and extract the lesson, run npm i. index.js has the Express setup, config with a bearer token placeholder, the index.ejs view with the five-button form, and a working /get-secret route. The other four routes are empty.
task.goal: Make POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE buttons each call the matching Secrets API endpoint and show the response (or error) in the content area, behaving like the instructor's solution.js demo.
steps: Run npm i, then paste the bearer token obtained in the previous (authentication) lesson into the yourBearerToken constant.
Start the app with nodemon and open localhost:3000. Optionally run solution.js first to see the target behaviour.
Study /get-secret: try/catch, await axios.get(url, config), render result.data stringified, render error.response.data on failure.
/post-secret: call axios.post(API_URL + '/secrets', req.body, config). The body is the form data (secret and score); no id needed since the API assigns it.
/put-secret: read req.body.id, then axios.put(API_URL + '/secrets/' + id, req.body, config).
/patch-secret: same shape as PUT but with axios.patch.
/delete-secret: read req.body.id and call axios.delete(API_URL + '/secrets/' + id, config); only two arguments, no body.

Test the whole lifecycle: POST a new secret (id 51), GET 51, PUT with full data, PATCH one field, DELETE, then GET 51 again to see the not-found error. Also try PUT on an id that does not exist to check error display.
task.expected_result: Each button displays the JSON returned by the API (created secret, updated secret, deletion confirmation). Invalid ids show the API's error text in the content box.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 28 - Aplication Programming Interfaces (APIs)/28.06 - REST APIs with Axios/solution.js

pitfalls: Forgetting to paste the bearer token (or leaving the placeholder) makes every route fail with an auth error.
Using the wrong arity: passing config as the second argument of axios.post/put/patch makes it be sent as the body; the body must come second and config third.
Forgetting the id in the URL for PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
PUT with missing fields wipes them; use PATCH for partial updates.
Accidentally committing a real bearer token (the reference repo shows one hard-coded; replace it with your own and keep it out of version control).
Not running npm i before starting the server.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (section 28 has no data file).
gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson: 'REST verbs with Axios'. Blurb: map GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to read/create/replace/update/remove and see how each Axios alias takes its arguments.

Tasks: (1) write get and delete calls with url + config; (2) write post with url + body + config; (3) show the difference between PUT and PATCH on a sample object; (4) convert a .then() chain to async/await with try/catch; (5) handle an error response by reading error.response.data.
Starter code idea: a mock in-browser 'secrets' store with fake fetch-like functions and a five-button form using formaction.

Interactive demo idea: a simulated API where the user edits id/secret/score, clicks a verb button, and sees the request line, body, and the resulting store state side by side, highlighting that PUT overwrites missing fields while PATCH keeps them.
